seed_ledger.name: Pine Prairie Energy Center Phase IV Storage Expansion
seed_ledger.reason: Storage cavern 6 (about 10 Bcf), a 19,000 HP electric compressor and about 2.37 miles of 30-inch header loop in Evangeline Parish, Louisiana. Williams (the owner) got FERC approval in May 2026 and plans service in the fourth quarter of 2028. Williams says the storage serves industrial, power and LNG demand. No source names a data center customer for this project, so it stays monitor with length known (2.4 mi). Searches run: 5. Sources: FERC notice of application and scoping (Aug-Sep 2025) showed the loop and compressor; FERC environmental assessment notice (Jan 2026) confirmed the same; FERC May 2026 meeting summary showed the certificate order in CP25-533; Williams second-quarter 2026 10-Q gave approval and the 2028 date; Williams earnings coverage said customer agreements are signed but did not name customers or data centers. Not run: air permit and county records.

evidence.note: Williams 10-Q for June 2026: FERC approval May 2026, Pine Prairie Phase IV storage and injection/withdrawal expansion
FERC environmental assessment notice, Pine Prairie Phase IV, Evangeline Parish

seed_ledger.name: Plantation North Expansion Gas Plant
seed_ledger.reason: A gas processing plant plus KinderHawk field gathering expansion in the northwest Louisiana Haynesville, which is gathering and processing, not transmission, and has no data center tie. Kinder Morgan's second-quarter 2026 call only says KinderHawk volumes rose 54 percent and a roughly 1 Bcf/d processing expansion is underway; no source names a Plantation North plant or a data center link. Searches run: 5. Sources: Kinder Morgan 10-K filings from 2011 and 2012 described KinderHawk as gathering only; trade press and the Q2 2026 call transcript showed volume growth only; Louisiana DEQ notices and processing-plant news showed no Plantation North entry. Drop stands.

seed_ledger.name: Pointe Coupee Power Station
seed_ledger.reason: NEW_LATERAL. Entergy Louisiana told the Louisiana Public Service Commission that a new gas pipeline has to be built for the three Pointe Coupee units. Who builds it, the route and the length are not public. Sources checked: Entergy direct testimony in the Meta docket (says pipeline costs and arrangements exist); Louisiana PSC testimony (units sit near the Big Cajun site); intervenor testimony and discovery (asks if the new pipeline needs FERC approval under the Natural Gas Act, and says the cost is spread on a system average basis); a general web search for FERC filings and open seasons for Big Cajun (nothing found); the newest federal pipeline projects workbook (no Pointe Coupee lateral found); trade press and local news (no route named). The 20-year Energy Transfer supply agreement in the same record is tied to other units, not shown to serve this plant. Searches run: 14. Consolidator check: no roster row starts or ends in Pointe Coupee Parish or at the Big Cajun site, so this is not a match to an existing row. The Alliance for Affordable Energy testimony of Edward Burgess in the same docket (July 31, 2026) says Entergy confirmed the Pointe Coupee units will likely need a new greenfield or brownfield pipeline.

evidence.note: Entergy testimony on pipeline costs for the Meta units, Pointe Coupee named
Units are near the Big Cajun site in Pointe Coupee Parish

candidates.researcher_notes: Not a match to any existing row. No row serves Pointe Coupee Parish or the Big Cajun site. Two Louisiana Public Service Commission documents in the Meta docket U-37882 load and name Pointe Coupee. One is Entergy Louisiana testimony that mentions pipeline costs and arrangements. Neither names who would build it, where it would run, or how long it would be. Earlier searches of the federal pipeline projects workbook, FERC filings and press found nothing. The Energy Transfer supply deal in the same docket is tied to other units. The data center link is Meta, but no source ties the pipeline itself to a stated route or builder, so the data center flag stays blank. Revisit if a FERC prefiling, a state permit or a named builder appears. Confidence is low.
